rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reports a plural reading, ālihatan hawāhu; Quraysh reportedly replaced al-ʿUzzā, a white stone, whenever they found a whiter, more attractive stone, supporting the plural, though the singular also fits.
rows.anchor: وقد رويت آلهة هواه، ولها وجه في التفسير وروي أن قريشا كانت تعبد العزى وهي حجر أبيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being led astray according to knowledge means God knew before creating the person that he would be astray.
rows.anchor: أي على ما سبق في علمه قبل أن يخلقه أنه ضال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for a covering over the sight is read either ghishwah, with fatḥa and no alif, or ghishāwah, with ḍamma and alif.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ غشوة بفتح الغين بغير ألف، ويقرأ غشاوة - بضم الغين والألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of “we die and live” is that some people die while their children or another generation lives; this does not affirm resurrection.
rows.anchor: يكون المعنى (نموت ونحيا)، يحيا أولادنا، فيموت قوم ويحيا قوم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation reverses no sequence: the coordinated verbs mean both dying and living, since waw does not show which comes first.
rows.anchor: ويكون معنى (نموت ونحيا) نحيا ونموت، لأن الواو للاجتماع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that humans began lifeless, then lived, and are finally destroyed by time.
rows.anchor: ويكون (نموت ونحيا وما يهلكنا إلا الدهر) أي ابتداؤنا موات في أصل الخلقة، ثم نحيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their assertion that worldly life is all there is shows they deny resurrection; God identifies their claim as error and conjecture without knowledge.
rows.anchor: المعنى ما هم إلا يظنون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With ḥujjatuhum nominative, it is kāna’s subject and “that they said” its predicate; the meaning is that their sole argument was their demand to bring back their fathers.
rows.anchor: يجوز في (حجتهم) الرفع، فمن رفع جعل (حجتهم) اسم كان و (أن قالوا) خبر كان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With ḥujjatuhum accusative, “that they said” is kāna’s subject; their only argument is the statement, “Bring our fathers.”
rows.anchor: ومن نصب (حجتهم) جعل اسم كان أن مع صلتها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes identify the resolute messengers as Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ومحمد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “a proclamation,” nominative balāgh means “that is a proclamation”; accusative balāghan is good Arabic but differs from the muṣḥaf, understood as “they attain a proclamation.”
rows.anchor: الرفع على معنى ذلك بلاغ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative is explained by an implicit verb, as in “God’s ordinance upon you,” understood as God prescribed it as an ordinance.
rows.anchor: على معنى يبلغون بلاغا كما قال: (كتاب الله عليكم) منصوب على معنى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given God’s mercy and bounty, only the sinful people perish; an alternate vocalized reading of the verb would be valid, though he knows no one who read it that way.
rows.anchor: تأويله أنه لا يهلك مع رحمة الله وتفضله إلا القوم الفاسقون ولو قرئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls this verse the strongest possible assurance of hope in God’s mercy.
rows.anchor: وما في الرجاء لرحمة الله شيء أقوى من هذه الآية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lughūb means fatigue or exhaustion; the verb is laghiba yalghabu lughūban.
rows.anchor: اللغوب: التعب والإعياء، يقال: لغب يلغب لغوبا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews reportedly claimed creation took six days, Sunday through Friday, and God rested on Saturday; the verse declares God far above fatigue or toil.
rows.anchor: قالت: خلق الله السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام أولها الأحد وآخرها الجمعة، واستراح يوم السبت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise before sunrise refers to the dawn prayer, and the praise before sunset to the afternoon prayer.
rows.anchor: يعني قبل طلوع الشمس صلاة الفجر، وقبل الغروب صلاة العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night praise refers to the sunset prayer; “after the prayers” may mean the two rakʿahs after Maghrib or praise after completing prayer.
rows.anchor: الركعتان بعد صلاة المغرب على هذا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading ad-bār has an open initial vowel and is the plural of dubur; id-bār is the verbal noun of adbara, “to depart.”
rows.anchor: بقتح الألف فهو جمع دبر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aǧāǧ is water so salty that it cannot be drunk; falawlā means “why not?” or “would that.”
rows.anchor: الأجاج الماء الملح الذي لا يمكن شربه ألبتة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tūrūna means you kindle or strike a fire: the fire drill catches, while awraytu means I caused the fire to ignite; Arabs rubbed two sticks together to make fire.
rows.anchor: تقول وري الزند يري وريا، فهو وار إذا انقدحت منه النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire reminds its viewer of Hell and its punishment, prompting remembrance of God and seeking refuge from Hell.
rows.anchor: أي إذا رآها الرائي ذكر جهنم وما يخافه من العذاب، فذكر الله عز وجل واستجار به منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muqwī is a traveler who comes to al-qawāʾ, a desolate, empty land.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (متاعا للمقوين)، المقوي الذي ينزل بالقواء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation, food, and drink collectively display God’s oneness, power, and blessings, so the command to glorify Him means to declare Him transcendent.
rows.anchor: مما يأكلون ويشربون، مما يدل على قدرته ووحدانيته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No, I swear” means “I swear”: lā strengthens the oath, as lā in li-allā yaʿlama means “so that the People of the Book may know.”
rows.anchor: ودخلت (لا) توكيدا كما قال عز وجل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stations of the stars are their setting places; compare the oath by the Lord of the easts and wests.
rows.anchor: كما قال - عز وجل - (فلا أقسم برب المشارق والمغارب).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the stars’ stations as the successive portions of Quranic revelation; the following oath and statement that it is a noble Quran support this view.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن مواقع النجوم يعنى به نجوم القرآن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf in kamathali is nominative as an adjective; the clause likens worldly life and its ornaments to rain and its growth.
rows.anchor: الكاف في موضع رفع من وجهين:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the kāf is nominative as a predicate after another predicate: worldly life and its adornment are like rain whose growth amazes people.
rows.anchor: ويكون رفعها على خبر بعد خبر، على معنى أن الحياة الدنيا وزينتها مثل غيث أعجب الكفار نباته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kuffār can mean cultivators: if even farmers are impressed by the crop, who know it well, its growth is exceptionally beautiful.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنه الزرع، وإذا أعجب الزراع نباته مع علمهم به، فهو في غاية ما يستحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-kuffār means those who disbelieve in God; they are more impressed by worldly adornment than believers.
rows.anchor: ويكون الكفار ههنا الكفار بالله، وهم أشد إعجابا بزينة الدنيا من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahīj means that the crop begins to dry and turn yellow; ḥuṭāman means shattered, broken, and gone, illustrating worldly life’s passing.
rows.anchor: (ثم يكون حطاما). أي متحطما متكسرا ذاهبا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riḍwān is also read riḍwān; ʿĀṣim is reported to have transmitted both the ḍamma and kasra forms, meaning forgiveness for God’s friends and punishment for His enemies.
rows.anchor: وقد روينا جميعا عن عاصم - بالضم والكسر -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Racing toward forgiveness and the Garden means competing through righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: المعنى سابقوا بالأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Gardens are variously said to number seven or four; the four-Garden view cites two Gardens for one who fears his Lord and two beneath them.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الجنات سبع، وقيل أربع لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the Garden’s width is stated; this exemplifies its size by the greatest measure people imagine, the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: وقيل عرضها ولم يذكر طولها - والله أعلم -

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd read “both are in the Fire, remaining therein”; this is valid Arabic but differs from the muṣḥaf. The standard accusative is a circumstantial accusative; the variant nominative is the predicate of inna.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن مسعود أنهما في النار خالدان فيها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the standard wording, ʿāqibatuhumā is kāna’s subject and “that both are in the Fire” its predicate; accusative ʿāqibatahumā is also read and is preferable, making innahumā the subject of kāna.
rows.anchor: والقراءة فكان عاقبتهما على اسم كان ويكون خبر كان أنهما في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tomorrow” means Judgment Day, brought close to people as though it were tomorrow; ghadan derives from ghaduww, normally written without the wāw in Quranic usage.
rows.anchor: أي ليوم القيامة، وقرب على الناس فجعل كأنه يأتي غدا.

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet retains the wāw in ghaduww, using ghaduwwan to mean a barren place the next day.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر في إثباتها: وما الناس إلا كالديار وأهلها. . .

rows.speaker: آخر
rows.claim: A second, unnamed poet also retains the wāw in ghaduww.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر: لا تغلواها وادلواها دلوا. . .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding threat refers also to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy; God will make His religion prevail and honor His Messenger and the believers.
rows.anchor: يعنون أيضا عبد الله بن أبي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God urges believers to maintain remembrance and not be miserly with their wealth; they should spend before death is unmistakably upon them.
rows.anchor: حضهم الله على إدامة الذكر له وأن لا يضنوا بأموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsīr says anyone who neglected zakat or pilgrimage asks for another chance when facing death.
rows.anchor: فجاء في التفسير أنه ما قصر أحد في الزكاة أو في الحج إلا سأل الكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading fa-aṣṣaddaq wa-akun makes the first verb a response to lawlā (“if only you delayed me”); akūn is jussive by coordination with that response’s syntactic position and conditional sense.
rows.anchor: جواب (لولا أخرتني) ومعناه هلا أخرتني.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading fa-aṣṣaddaq wa-akūna follows the overt form of the first verb, with both verbs in the same mood.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ وأكون فهو على لفظ (فأصدق) وأكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light sent down by God is the Quran, a clear Book.
rows.anchor: أي وبالقرآن الذي هو نور وكتاب مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawma is an adverb linked to the promise that people will be resurrected and told what they did: on the day of gathering.
rows.anchor: (يوم) منصوب بقوله (لتبعثن ثم لتنبؤن بما عملتم) يوم الجمع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Mutual Loss is when the people of Paradise gain over the people of the Fire and higher-ranked residents of Paradise gain over those below them.
rows.anchor: ويوم التغابن يوم يغبن أهل الجنة أهل النار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This loss is illustrated as a commercial bargain: faith and the purchase of guidance bring salvation, unlike those who bought misguidance.
rows.anchor: وضرب ذلك مثلا للشراء والبيع كما قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If mothers nurse the children, they are to be paid their nursing wages.
rows.anchor: (فإن أرضعن لكم فآتوهن أجورهن). أي فأعطوهن أجرة رضاعهن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret mutual agreement in fairness as clothing and covering; he prefers fair support for a nursing mother, especially the child’s own mother, who is more compassionate, with both parents cooperating for the child.
rows.anchor: قيل في التفسير إنه الكسوة والدثار، والمعروف - والله أعلم -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If parents cannot agree, another woman will nurse; the future declarative wording conveys a command, as in the command for mothers to nurse for two full years.
rows.anchor: معناه فليرضع الوالد غير والدة الصبي، وهذا خبر في معنى الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affluent should provide nursing mothers according to their means; someone with only subsistence should spend accordingly, as the rule for the affluent and constrained states.
rows.anchor: أمر أهل التوسعة أن يوسعوا على نسائهم المرضعات أولادهن على قدر سعتهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “what He has given her” means what God has bestowed upon her.
rows.anchor: (لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا ما آتاها) أي إلا ما أعطاها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Muslims were poor and needy in the Prophet’s time; God promised relief, and later opened conquests brought ease after hardship.
rows.anchor: ففتح الله عليهم بعد ذلك وجعل يسرا بعد عسر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hastened punishment upon a defiant town; the wording attributes the act to the town while meaning its inhabitants were reckoned and punished.
rows.anchor: أي عجلنا لها العذاب، ومعناه: عتا أهلها فحاسبنا أهلها وعذبناهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outcome was a heavy consequence and loss in the Hereafter, namely the severe punishment prepared for them.
rows.anchor: يعني في الآخرة وهو قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admonition calls the believers to affirm the Prophet and follow his command; God sent the Messenger to lead people from darkness to light. Ulū al-albāb are people of intellect, each a possessor of intellect.
rows.anchor: ثم وعظ الله هذه الأمة في تصديق النبي عليه السلام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best parsing of rasūlan supplies an implicit arsala, “He sent a Messenger to recite”; the preceding mention of a Reminder cues it.
rows.anchor: (قد أنزل الله إليكم ذكرا) دليلا على إضمار أرسل رسولا يتلو عليكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, rasūlan refers to the Prophet and is governed by dhikran, “a renowned Reminder, a Messenger who recites.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون يعني بقوله (رسولا) النبي عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parsing makes rasūlan an appositive to dhikran and identifies the Messenger as Gabriel; the evidence is that the Trustworthy Spirit brought it to the Prophet’s heart.
rows.anchor: ويكون (رسولا) بدلا من ذكر، ويكون يعنى به جبريل عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden was an orchard in Yemen. Its former owner kept his annual food and gave the surplus to the poor; reports also describe generous gleanings left for them, which accumulated substantially.
rows.anchor: والجنة: البستان، وهؤلاء قوم بناحية اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons feared that continuing their father’s charity would leave too little for their group, so they swore to harvest at night and omitted “if God wills.”
rows.anchor: فقال بنوه: نحن جماعة، وإن فعلنا بالمساكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥard is linked to a year withholding its yield; another interpretation takes it as anger.
rows.anchor: من قولهم: حاردت السنة إذا منعت خيرها.

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An anonymous poetic line uses ḥard to mean setting out toward or aiming for a fertile garden.
rows.anchor: فأما الحرد الذي هو القصد فأنشدوا فيه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A heavenly punishment swept over the garden and burned all of it.
rows.anchor: أي أرسل عليها عذابا من السماء فاحترقت كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden became black as night.
rows.anchor: أي فأصبحت كالليل سوادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called one another early, urging each other to go to their crop if they intended to harvest it.
rows.anchor: أي إن كنتم عازمين على صرام النخل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They whispered among themselves that no needy person should enter the garden; takhāfut means speaking secretly.
rows.anchor: أي يسرون الكلام بينهم بأن: (لا يدخلنها اليوم عليكم مسكين).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the burned garden, they first thought they had lost their way and this was not their orchard, then recognized it as punishment.
rows.anchor: محترقة. (قالوا إنا لضالون)، أي قد ضللنا طريق جنتنا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were deprived of the garden’s fruit because they had withheld it from the poor.
rows.anchor: أي حرمنا ثمر جنتنا بمنعنا المساكين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their middle brother was the fairest; wasaṭ is glossed as just, as in the justly balanced community.
rows.anchor: (أوسطهم) أعدلهم من قوله: (وكذلك جعلناكم أمة وسطا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ here means making an exception to the oath by saying in shāʾ Allāh. Though tasbīḥ can mean “Glory be to God,” any magnification of God counts; the exception acknowledges that action depends on His will.
rows.anchor: ومعنى التسبيح ههنا الاستثناء، وهو أن يقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ linguistically means declaring God free of evil; an oath’s exception magnifies God and admits that no act occurs apart from His will.
rows.anchor: لأن التسبيح في اللغة فيما جاء عن النبي عليه السلام تنزيه الله عن السوء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden story also exemplifies God’s trial of Mecca: after the Prophet prayed against Muḍar for years of hardship like Joseph’s, God afflicted them with disease, death, and lost provisions.
rows.anchor: فقال: اللهم اشدد وطأتك على مضر واجعلها عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell calls the disbeliever and hypocrite by name.
rows.anchor: تدعو الكافر باسمه والمنافق باسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Halūʿ describes a person who fears and grieves at evil, as the verse’s interpretation says.
rows.anchor: الهلوع على ما في الآية من التفسير يفزع ويجزع من الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The human” means people generally; the exception is believers who pray and persist in prayer, meaning those who guard the obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: يعني به المحافظين على الصلاة المكتوبة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the constant worshippers never turn away from the direction of prayer or look around; dāʾim can mean stationary, as in still water.
rows.anchor: فيكون اشتقاقه من الدائم وهو الساكن، كما جاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A deprived person is one whose earnings are blocked; he does not ask others.
rows.anchor: قد حرم المكاسب. وهو لا يسأل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical account understands ʿalā as min, so the exception means “except from their spouses or those their right hands possess.”
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها في معنى " من " المعنى عند قائل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, retain ʿalā by construing the sense as “they are not blameworthy concerning their spouses”; the following clause supports it.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن " على " محمول على المعنى، المعنى فإنهم لا يلامون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking God as wakīl means taking Him as guarantor of what He promised.
rows.anchor: أي اتخذه كفيلا بما وعدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction to bear patiently and withdraw graciously indicates that this came before Muslims were commanded to fight.
rows.anchor: هذا يدل - والله أعلم -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Leave Me with the deniers” is an Arabic idiom: it means do not concern yourself with them, since God will take care of them, not that anything restrains God.
rows.anchor: تأويله لا تهتم بزيد فإني أكفيكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ankāl is the plural of nikl; tafsīr identifies them here as fiery restraints.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أنه ههنا قيود من نار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choking food is ḍarīʿ, also identified as shibriq, a thorn like ʿawsaj; another verse says they have no food but ḍarīʿ.
rows.anchor: وهو الشبرق، وهو شوك كالعوسج.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fire in this world serves as a reminder of the Fire in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن النار في الدنيا تذكر بالنار في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both adbara and dubira are sound Arabic for night’s departure; similarly, night may be said to approach or come.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (إذ دبر)، وكلاهما جيد في العربية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading has alif in both phrases: idhā adbara and al-ṣubḥ idhā asfara.
rows.anchor: وقد قرئت أيضا (إذا أدبر) (والصبح إذا أسفر).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to Hell: it is great in its role as a warning. Nadhīran is accusative as a circumstantial expression and masculine because its sense is punishment.
rows.anchor: هذه الهاء كناية عن النار، أي إنها لكبيرة في حال الإنذار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadhīran may instead be masculine by analogy with a woman called ṭāhir or ṭāliq, meaning one possessing purity or divorce, hence “possessing warning.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التذكير على قولهم امرأة طاهر وطالق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, nadhīran can attach to the opening of the sūra: “arise as a warner to humankind.”
rows.anchor: معلقا بأول السورة على معنى قم نذيرا للبشر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To advance or fall back means to advance in what was commanded or to lag behind; the warning has already been delivered.
rows.anchor: فيما أمر به أو يتأخر، فقد أنذرتم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Has there come” means “has there not come”; one reading concerns a person who was dust and clay, not mentioned before the spirit was breathed into him.
rows.anchor: ألم يأت على الإنسان حين من الدهر، - وقد كان شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse concerns all people, who passed through sperm, clot, and morsel stages before becoming mentionable.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون يعنى به جميع الناس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hal atā also has the completed sense “it has come upon the human.”
rows.anchor: ومعنى (هل أتى) قد أتى على الإنسان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amshāj means mixtures of semen and blood, moving from one stage to another; its singular is mishīj.
rows.anchor: (أمشاج) أخلاط مني ودم، ثم ينقل من حال إلى حال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabtalī means “test”; the fact that God made the human hearing and seeing demonstrates this testing purpose.
rows.anchor: يدل عليه: (فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣīl means evening; aṣalnā means they entered the evening.
rows.anchor: يقال: قد أصلنا إذا دخلوا في الأصيل، وهو العشي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asruhum means their creation; tafsīr also glosses it as their joints.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أيضا مفاصلهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People can will only what God wills.
rows.anchor: أي لستم تشاءون إلا بمشيئة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative al-ẓālimīn continues an implicit object: God admits whom He wills to mercy and punishes the wrongdoers; aʿadda lahum explains the omitted verb.
rows.anchor: المعنى يدخل من يشاء في رحمته ويعذب الظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative al-ẓālimūn is possible as a subject with the following clause as predicate, but he rejects it because it differs from the muṣḥaf and Basran grammarians prefer the accusative as the stronger construction.
rows.anchor: ولا أرى القراءة بها، من وجهين:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basran grammarians prefer the accusative, as in coordinating ʿAmr as an object and then explaining that one prepared good for him; Quranic reading should use the best construction matching the muṣḥaf.
rows.anchor: فإن الاختيار عند النحويين البصريين النصب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-arḍ is read accusative by supplying “and He spread the earth after that,” with daḥāhā explaining the omitted verb; this is preferable to nominative as a topic because verb coordinates with verb, as in “He built it.”
rows.anchor: على معنى: ودحا الأرض بعد ذلك، وفسر هذا المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nominative reading of al-arḍ as the topic is also reported.
rows.anchor: وقد قرئت (والأرض بعد ذلك دحاها) على الرفع بالابتداء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains can likewise be parsed accusatively by supplying an omitted verb or nominatively; the accusative is interpreted like the earth, and arsāhā means He fixed them firmly.
rows.anchor: تفسير نصب الجبال كتفسير نصب الأرض، وكذلك يجوز الرفع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿan is accusative as a verbal noun of purpose: God brought out water and pasture for people and their livestock to enjoy.
rows.anchor: نصب (متاعا لكم) بمعنى قوله أخرج منها ماءها ومرعاها للإمتاع لكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Great Calamity is the blast that overwhelms everything and brings resurrection, judgment, punishment, torment, and mercy.
rows.anchor: إذا جاءت الصيحة التي تطم كل شيء، الصيحة التي يقع معها البعث والحساب والعقاب والعذاب والرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to “when the Great Calamity comes” is that the outcome is as stated: for the transgressor who preferred worldly life, Hell is his refuge.
rows.anchor: فإن الأمر كذلك، ومعنى هي المأوى أي هي المأوى له،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the article al- as replacing the possessive pronoun, so al-maʾwā means “his refuge”; the vocative command “lower the gaze, man” likewise means “your gaze,” as in the poet’s line.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: الألف واللام بدل من الهاء، المعنى فهي مأواه

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet’s “lower the gaze” addresses a man whose gaze is meant; this supports reading al-maʾwā as “his refuge” for both Hell and Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: فغض الطرف إنك من نمير. . . فلا كعبا بلغت ولا كلابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyāna means “when,” asking the time of the Hour’s occurrence and arising.
rows.anchor: معناه متى وقوعها وقيامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour’s endpoint with the Lord means that the limit of knowledge about it belongs to Him.
rows.anchor: أي منتهى علمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nunation, mundhir describes present warning or future warning; active participles for present or future are indefinite like verbs. Nunation may be omitted at a resumption, though its meaning remains understood; a past warning is unnunated.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (منذر) بالتنوين على معنى إنما أنت في حال إنذار من يخشاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ʿashiyyatan aw ḍuḥāhā, the final alif and hāʾ refer to ʿashiyyah: “an evening or its forenoon,” with the forenoon annexed to the evening.
rows.anchor: هذه الألف والهاء عائدة على (عشية)، المعنى إلا عشية أو ضحاها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning, evening, and forenoon belong to their day: “morning and its evening” is followed by that day’s evening, whereas “evening and its morning” means the following morning.
rows.anchor: والغداة والعشي والضحوة والضحى لليوم الذي يكون فيه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿan is an emphatic verbal noun for the preceding “We caused to grow”: producing these things benefits humankind and all animals.
rows.anchor: منصوب، مصدر مؤكد لقوله (فأنبتنا فيها)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṣākhkhah is the blast at resurrection; it deafens ears so that one hears only the call summoning people to life.
rows.anchor: التي تكون عليها القيامة، تصخ الأسماع أي تصمها فلا يسمع إلا ما يدعى فيه لإحيائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day the blast comes is when each person flees relatives, since each person is consumed by a concern that absorbs him.
rows.anchor: (يوم يفر المرء من أخيه (34) وأمه وأبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading yughnihi means his concern preoccupies him; yuʿnīhi is also read, meaning it concerns him. Either way, he cannot attend to anyone else.
rows.anchor: بالغين معجمة، وقد قرئت (شأن يعنيه)،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The radiant faces are illuminated because they know the victory and bliss awaiting them.
rows.anchor: (مسفرة) مضيئة قد علمت ما لها من الفوز والنعيم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other faces are covered in dust and overlaid with blackness like smoke.
rows.anchor: أي غبرة يعلوها سواد كالدخان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with these faces are the disbelieving sinners.
rows.anchor: (أولئك هم الكفرة الفجرة (42).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khunnas, jawārī, and kunnas are plural forms; lā strengthens the oath, whose first sense is “I swear.” Most interpreters take the terms as stars that run, disappear, and set in their places.
rows.anchor: الخنس جمع خانس، والجواري جمع جارية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is wild cattle and gazelles: they are snub-nosed, and kunnas describes them entering a thicket or tree branch as shelter.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخنس ههنا يعني بقر الوحش وظباء الوحش،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asʿasa can mean that night approaches or departs; both meanings relate to the beginning of darkness, at its onset or when it recedes at the end.
rows.anchor: يقال عسعس الليل إذا أقبل، وعسعس إذا أدبر، والمعنيان يرجعان إلى شيء واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn “breathes” when it spreads until daylight is clear.
rows.anchor: إذا امتد حتى يصير نهارا بينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s first answer says the Quran is the speech of a noble messenger, meaning Gabriel brought it down.
rows.anchor: وجواب القسم في هذه الأشياء أعني (فلا أقسم بالخنس)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel’s strength was shown when he overturned Lot’s four towns with the tips of his wings.
rows.anchor: أنه قلب مدينة قوم لوط بقوادم جناحه وهي قرى أربع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your companion is not mad” is another answer to the oath, referring to the Prophet; the Quran was brought by Gabriel, and the Prophet saw him at the clear horizon, explained earlier in Sūrat al-Najm.
rows.anchor: هذا أيضا جواب القسم، المعنى فأقسم بهذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-shafaq is the red glow seen in the western horizon after sunset; another view identifies it as daytime.
rows.anchor: والشفق الحمرة التي ترى في الأفق في المغرب بعد سقوط الشمس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasaqa means gathered and joined together; a poet’s mustawsiqāt illustrates things gathered together.
rows.anchor: معنى وسق جمع وضم. قال الشاعر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon has gathered and become full on the thirteenth or fourteenth night.
rows.anchor: اجتمع واستوى ليلة ثلاث عشرة وأربعة عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading, layarkabanna, means people will pass through one state after another—revival, death, and resurrection—until they reach God.
rows.anchor: أي حالا بعد حال حتى يصير إلى الله عز وجل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading, latarkabunna, addresses Muhammad: he will pass from one level of heaven to another.
rows.anchor: وقرئت: (لتركبن طبقا عن طبق).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yūʿūn means what people carry in their hearts; compare placing goods in a container and retaining knowledge.
rows.anchor: أي بما يحملون في قلوبهم، يقال: أوعيت المتاع في الوعاء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For disbelievers, give the opposite of glad tidings: the painful punishment instead of the believers’ Garden, mercy, and good pleasure.
rows.anchor: المعنى اجعل بدل البشارة للمؤمنين بالجنة والرحمة والرضوان، للكفار العذاب الأليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr mamnūn means an unmerited reward for which they are not reproached; another view means it is uncut or unending, as manaytu means I cut the rope.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: غير ممنون غير مقطوع، يقال منيت الحبل إذا قطعته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamman means abundant; turāth derives from wirāth, with tāʾ replacing wāw when the wāw is ḍamma, as in wijāh becoming tijāh.
rows.anchor: ولكن التاء تبدل من الواو إذا كانت الواو مضمومة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is shaken and its parts crush one another.
rows.anchor: إذا زلزلت فدك بعضها بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The angels” explains the singular al-malak collectively, as in the verse about God and the angels coming under clouds.
rows.anchor: كما قال جل ثناوة: (هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله في ظلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is brought forth, as in the statement that it was exposed to the sinners; tafsīr says it is dragged by a million reins, each held by seventy thousand angels.
rows.anchor: وقيل في التفسير جيء بجهنم تقاد بألف زمام كل زمام في أيدي سبعين ألف ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day people display repentance; “how could he remember?” means “how could he repent then?”
rows.anchor: أي ومن أين له الذكرى، أي التوبة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His “life” is the abode of the Hereafter, where there is no death.
rows.anchor: أي لدار الآخرة التي لا موت فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading means no one is punished with a punishment like that of this disbeliever or his kind.
rows.anchor: المعنى لا يعذب عذاب هذا الكافر وعذاب هذا الصنف من الكفار أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more common active reading means that no one administers God’s punishment on Judgment Day, when sovereignty belongs to God alone; another view says no worldly punishment equals God’s punishment in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (لا يعذب)، وهو أكثر القراءة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parent and child are interpreted as Adam and his descendants, or more generally as every parent and child.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن معناه آدم وولده، وجاء معناه أيضا كل والد وكل مولود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s answer says humans were created amid hardship, struggling in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: هذا جواب القسم، المعنى أقسم بهذه الأشياء (لقد خلقنا الإنسان في كبد)،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes kabad as being created upright, walking on two legs unlike other creatures.
rows.anchor: وقيل: (في كبد) أي خلق منتصبا يمشي على رجليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view describes the fetus’s head as first aligned with its mother’s, then turning downward before birth.
rows.anchor: وقيل (في كبد) خلق الإنسان في بطن أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsīr identifies a powerful man, Kulda, who stood on a leather mat and stamped it into scraps; the challenge asks whether he thought strength kept anyone from overpowering or resurrecting him.
rows.anchor: كان شديدا جدا، وكان يبسط له الأديم العكاظي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he thought no one, meaning God, could overpower him because he denied resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل أن لن يقدر عليه الله عز وجل لأنه كان لا يؤمن بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labad means much, packed or stuck together; labad is also read as the plural of lābid.
rows.anchor: كثير بعضه قد لبد ببعض، وفعل للكثرة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He thinks no one saw him means he thinks no one recorded his spending; his claim suggests that he said he spent much without benefit.
rows.anchor: أي أيحسب أن لم يحص عليه ما أنفق، وفي الكلام دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eyes, tongue, lips, and guidance to the two paths show that God can resurrect a person and reckon his deeds.
rows.anchor: ما يسستدل به على أن الله قادر على أن يبعثه وأن يحصي عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-najdayn are the two clear paths; najd is elevated ground, and the image means God made the paths of good and evil plain like two raised roads.
rows.anchor: الطريقين الواضحين، النجد المرتفع من الأرض، فالمعنى ألم نعرفه طريق الخير وطريق الشر بينين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falā iqtahama means “he did not climb”; it is like falā ṣaddaqa wa-lā ṣallā, with a second lā understood because “then he was among the believers” implies he neither surmounted the obstacle nor believed.
rows.anchor: المعنى فلم يقتحم العقبة كما قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic usually repeats lā in such constructions: “lā ḥayyaytanī” alone rarely means “as long as you leave me alive”; “you neither greeted me nor visited me” is well formed.
rows.anchor: وقلما يتكلم العرب في مثل هذا المكان إلا بلا مرتين أو أكثر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading gives the verbal nouns “freeing a neck or feeding during a day of hunger”; another reads “free a neck, or feed.” Both are valid: the first explains surmounting the obstacle, the second follows the contextual sense.
rows.anchor: وقرئت: (فك رقبة (13) أو إطعام في يوم ذي مسغبة (14)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masghabah means famine.
rows.anchor: والمسغبة المجاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhā maqrabah means a person with kinship; dhū qarābatī or dhū maqribatī is acceptable, while Zayd qarābatī is awkward because qarābah is a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: معناه ذا قرابة، تقول زيد ذو قرابتي وذو مقربتي، وزيد قرابتي قبيح لأن القرابة المصدر

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet’s line uses dhū qarābatihi for a relative, witnessing the construction with dhū.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: يبكي عليه غريب ليس يعرفه. . .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhā matrabah describes someone so poor that he is stuck to the dirt.
rows.anchor: يعنى أنه من فقره قد لصق بالتراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person first does these deeds while holding the bond of faith, then remains steadfast in faith; mutual counsel means patience in obedience and away from sin, and compassion.
rows.anchor: معناه إذا فعل ذلك وكان عقد الإيمان ثم أقام على إيمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the right are fortunate with respect to themselves, not ill-omened.
rows.anchor: أولئك أصحاب اليمن على أنفسهم أي كانوا ميامين على أنفسهم غير مشائيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the left are ill-omened toward themselves; he seeks refuge from the Fire.
rows.anchor: أي هم المشائيم على أنفسهم، نعوذ بالله من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s answer is “the one who purifies it succeeds,” meaning “has indeed succeeded”; the long intervening speech replaces the omitted lām.
rows.anchor: هذا قسم وجوابه: (قد أفلح من زكاها).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍuḥāhā means the sun’s light; another view takes it as daytime.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (وضحاها) وضيائها. وقيل ضحاها النهار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash and his companions read ḍuḥāhā, talāhā, and ṭaḥāhā with fatḥa, then the rest of the sūra with kasra; al-Kisāʾī uses imālah throughout and Abū ʿAmr a midpoint pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وأصحابه ضحاها وتلاها وطحاها بالفتح، وقرأوا باقي السورة بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people call kasra is imālah, per al-Khalīl and Abū ʿAmr: it signals roots with yāʾ. Fatḥa reflects these roots’ wāw origin, while wāw roots shift to yāʾ in passive forms such as tuliya, duḥiya, and ṭuḥiya.
rows.anchor: هذا الذي يسميه الناس الكسر ليس بكسر صحيح، يسميه الخليل وأبو عمرو الإمالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon follows the sun “when” it follows; another explanation is that the moon becomes full and follows the sun in brightness and light.
rows.anchor: وقيل حين - استدار فكان يتلو الشمس في الضياء والنور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day reveals the darkness, which is understood though unstated, like saying “our morning became cold”; alternatively, daylight reveals the sun as it spreads.
rows.anchor: قالوا معناه إذا جلى الظلمة، وإن لم يكن في الكلام ذكر الظلمة فالمعنى يدل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The sky and what built it” can mean the sky and its building, likewise earth and its spreading and the soul and its proportioning; alternatively, mā means “the one who,” as in Hijaz usage “glory to the one you glorified.”
rows.anchor: معناه والسماء وبنائها، وكذلك (والأرض وما طحاها) معناه والأرض وطحوها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by these mighty created things because they demonstrate that He is one and nothing resembles Him.
rows.anchor: بهذه الأشياء العظام من خلقه لأنها تدل على أنه واحد والذي ليس كمثله شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍuḥā means daytime, or one period within the day.
rows.anchor: والضحى: النهار، وقيل ساعة من ساعات النهار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sajā means that the night became still; the poet’s al-layl al-sāj uses sāj for stillness.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: يا حبذا القمراء والليل الساج. . .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God neither stopped sending revelation nor hated the Prophet. Revelation paused for fifteen days, prompting people to say his companion had forsaken and hated him; the verse answered them.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه تأخر الوحي عن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - خمسة عشر يوما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object “you” is omitted after qalā, as in the feminine form of “those who remember God often,” which likewise implies the object.
rows.anchor: كما قال: (والذاكرين الله كثيرا والذاكرات) المعنى والذاكراته (1).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s uncle Abū Ṭālib took care of him.
rows.anchor: وكان النبي عليه السلام يكفله عمه أبو طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening the Prophet’s chest means that God opened it to Islam.
rows.anchor: أي شرحناه للإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laying aside the burden means God forgave the Prophet’s earlier and later sins.
rows.anchor: أي وضعنا عنك إثمك أن غفر الله لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised the Prophet’s renown by joining it with the declaration of His oneness in the call to prayer and other frequent remembrances.
rows.anchor: جعل ذكر رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - مقرونا بذكر توحيد الله في الأذان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because al-ʿusr is repeated with the definite article, it is the same hardship, while the repeated indefinite yusr denotes two eases; the Prophet said one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: فذكر العسر مع الألف واللام ثم ثنى ذكره، فصار المعنى إن مع العسر يسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying holds that if hardship entered a hole, ease would follow it; the Companions were in severe straits, and God promised relief and opened conquests for them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لو دخل العسر جحرا لدخل اليسر عليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-tīn and al-zaytūn are variously interpreted as Damascus and Jerusalem; the mountains above those cities; two mountains; or the familiar fig and olive fruits.
rows.anchor: قيل التين دمشق والزيتون بيت المقدس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read ṭūr Sīnāʾ rather than ṭūr Sīnīn; he prefers that interpretation because another verse mentions a tree growing from Mount Sinai.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول - والله أعلم - أشبه لقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure city is Mecca.
rows.anchor: يعني مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human was created in the best form.
rows.anchor: أي في أحسن صورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of being returned to the lowest of the low is decrepit old age.
rows.anchor: إلى أرذل العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is misguidance, supported by the statement that humanity is in loss except those who believe and do good.
rows.anchor: وقيل إلى الضلال كما قال عز وجل: (إن الإنسان لفي خسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers that humanity was created upon the natural disposition, and whoever disbelieves and strays is returned to the lowest of the low.
rows.anchor: وهو - والله أعلم - أن خلق الخلق على الفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe and act righteously are excluded from that decline.
rows.anchor: أي إلا هؤلاء فلم يردوا إلى أسفل سافلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr mamnūn means that no one reproaches them for the reward; another view means the reward is not cut off.
rows.anchor: أي لا يمن عليهم، وقيل غير ممنون غير مقطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by the fig and olive is answered by the statement that God created humanity in the best form.
rows.anchor: وجواب القسم في قوله: (والتين والزيتون) قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāriʿah, Wāqiʿah, and Ḥāqqah are descriptions of the Hour; al-qāriʿah strikes with terrors.
rows.anchor: القارعة والواقعة والحاقة من صفات ساعة القيامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawma is an adverb: “the day when people are like scattered moths”; people swarm like locusts at resurrection, moving over one another.
rows.anchor: (يوم) منصوب على الظرف، المعنى يكون يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moths are small insects that rush into fire; people at resurrection are compared to scattered, swarming locusts.
rows.anchor: وشبه الناس في وقت البعث بالجراد المنتشر، والفراش المبثوث لأنهم إذا بعثوا يموج بعضهم في بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIhn means wool; its singular is ʿihnah, as ṣūfah relates to ṣūf.
rows.anchor: (العهن) الصوف، واحدته عهنة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavy scales mean abundant good deeds, like saying someone has great weight with me; a pleasing life is a life its inhabitant approves.
rows.anchor: معناه من ثقلت موازينه بالحسنات، كما تقول: لفلان عندي وزن ثقيل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some gloss rāḍiyah as “pleasing,” which returns to the same exegetical meaning: a life that satisfies its inhabitant.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: معناه مرضية، وهو يعود إلى هذا المعنى في التفسير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ummuhu hāwiyah means his dwelling is Hell; “mother” names the place one settles toward, which is then specified as a burning fire.
rows.anchor: أي فمسكنه النار. وقيل (أمه) لمسكنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pause at hiyah; when connected, read hiya nārun ḥāmiyah. The pause hāʾ clarifies the yāʾ’s vowel, and the written muṣḥaf requires retaining and pausing on it.
rows.anchor: الوقف " هيه "، والوصل هي نار حامية إلا أن الهاء دخلت في الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Competition for money and children distracted people from obeying God.
rows.anchor: أي شغلكم التكاثر بالأموال والأولاد عن طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Visiting the graves means death caught them in that state.
rows.anchor: أي حتى أدرككم الموت على تلك الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two Arab clans, Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm, boasted by counting the living; after ʿAbd Manāf outnumbered them, Sahm challenged them to count the dead and then surpassed them.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن حيين من العرب، وهم بنو عبد مناف وبنو سهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā is a rebuke and warning: competing for abundance is not the proper course; obedience to God and belief in His Prophet are.
rows.anchor: (كلا) ردع وتنبيه، المعنى ليس الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIlm al-yaqīn is knowing something with true certainty and directing one’s understanding to it; that knowledge would restrain them.
rows.anchor: المعنى لو علمتم الشيء حق علمه، وصرفتم التفهم إليه، لارتدعتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat that they will see Hell is compared to the statement that all people will come to it.
rows.anchor: كما قال: (وإن منكم إلا واردها).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prevalent reading of latarawunna has an unhamzated wāw; some hamza it, though grammarians avoid hamza where the wāw’s ḍamma arose only to separate two vowelless letters.
rows.anchor: وقد همزها بعضهم - لترؤن - والنحويون يكرهون همزة الواو،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians allow either hamza or no hamza when wāw’s ḍamma is inherent, as in adʾur or adūr, but prefer no hamza in latarawunnahā; a passive reading latarʾawunna is also reported.
rows.anchor: ويهمزون الواو التي ضمتها لازمة نحو أدؤر جمع دار، فيجوز أدؤر بالهمز وادور بغير الهمز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day people are questioned about every worldly comfort.
rows.anchor: أي يوم القيامة، عن كل ما يتنعم به في الدنيا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet and companions ate dates—or, in another transmission, fresh dates—and drank water, then praised God for food, drink, and Islam.
rows.anchor: أكل هو وجماعة من أصحابه تمرا - وروي بسرا - وشربوا عليه ماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report exempts clothing that covers nakedness, food sufficient to support the back, and shelter from heat and cold from the questioning.
rows.anchor: وطعاما يقيم به صلبه، ومكانا يكنه من الحر والبرد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses refer to hypocrites who pray only when believers see them and skip prayer when unseen.
rows.anchor: يعنى بهذا المنافقون، لأنهم كانوا إنما يراءون بالصلاة إذا هم رآهم المؤمنون صلوا معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says they are heedless because they delay prayer past its time; whoever deliberately delays until the next prayer time begins also faces woe.
rows.anchor: ومن تعمد تأخيرها عن وقتها حتى يدخل وقت غيرها فالويل له أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-māʿūn means things that are useful.
rows.anchor: أي يمنعون ما فيه منفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic usage, māʿūn included any useful item, even an axe, bucket, pot, or fire striker—anything useful, little or much; al-Aʿshā’s poem uses the word māʿūnihi.
rows.anchor: والماعون في الجاهلية ما فيه منفعة حتى الفأس والدلو والقدر والقداحة

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line witnesses māʿūn as a useful possession or provision offered generously.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى: بأجود منه بماعونه. . . إذا ما سماؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Islam, māʿūn is said to mean zakat and obedience; al-Rāʿī’s verse mentions people withholding their māʿūn and neglecting the declaration of God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: والماعون في الإسلام قيل هو الزكاة والطاعة. قال الراعي.

rows.speaker: الراعي
rows.claim: Al-Rāʿī’s poem uses māʿūnahum while describing people who withhold it and neglect tahlīl, supporting the gloss of ritual obligation and obedience.
rows.anchor: قال الراعي. قومي على الإسلام لما يمنعوا. . . ماعونهم
